topic: Role Models, Mentorship, and Community: Advancing Women in the Chemical Sciences
title: Role Models, Mentorship, and Community: Advancing Women in the Chemical Sciences
session_title: Emerging Stars: Elevating Early-Career Voices in Chemical Engineering through Innovation and Mentorship (Invited Talks)
abstract: Encouraging women in chemical sciences requires both inspiration and persistence. This presentation will explore initiatives that encourage women at all stages: early exposure to science, mentoring in higher education, and leadership development in professional and academic settings. I will share lessons learned from addressing imposter phenomenon, building community through women-in-chemistry and chemical engineering events, and translating technical expertise into purposeful advocacy. This perspective underscores how intentional engagement can help ensure a diverse, innovative, and resilient workforce for the future of the chemical sciences.

topic: AI Research and Teaching Assistants As Thought Partners
title: AI Research and Teaching Assistants As Thought Partners
session_title: Emerging Stars: Elevating Early-Career Voices in Chemical Engineering through Innovation and Mentorship (Invited Talks)
abstract: Imagine an engineering textbook that explains student questions on demand, viz. "Can you provide another explanation of entropy? I don't quite understand." Imagine a trained and knowledgeable research mentor and coach that provides you with critical feedback on likely gaps before you submit a proposal. This presentation will give an overview of how to create AI assistants that are trained to score draft proposals with a technical persona trained in your research field, coach trainees, and provide interactive feedback on a closed knowledge set for on-boarding and professional development.

title: Keys to Authentic Leadership
session_title: Emerging Stars: Elevating Early-Career Voices in Chemical Engineering through Innovation and Mentorship (Invited Talks)
abstract: There are more ways to prove and develop your leadership experience in your early career beyond managing direct reports at work. It's about showcasing the impact you generated in any environment. Come and hear a first-hand example of how to maximize your leadership potential, along with tips to become a better leader.

topic: Decades of Entrepreneurship and Leadership: Shaping Innovation and Growth
title: Decades of Entrepreneurship and Leadership: Shaping Innovation and Growth
session_title: Emerging Stars: Elevating Early-Career Voices in Chemical Engineering through Innovation and Mentorship (Invited Talks)
abstract: Over the past decades, entrepreneurship and leadership have been central forces in shaping innovation and driving economic growth. Drawing on lessons from decades of experience, I will highlight how we, as chemical engineers, create value by fostering innovation ecosystems, mobilizing resources, and building networks that accelerate the commercialization of processes, products, and technologies. I will illustrate how cultivating vision, embracing risk, learning from failure, and leading with purpose, all entrepreneurial behavior, are vital for today’s rapidly changing landscape and foundational for shaping innovation.

topic: Expanding Impact through Outreach and Education: Early-Career Perspectives
title: Expanding Impact through Outreach and Education: Early-Career Perspectives
session_title: Emerging Stars: Elevating Early-Career Voices in Chemical Engineering through Innovation and Mentorship (Invited Talks)
abstract: Outreach and teaching provide powerful platforms for connecting chemical engineering with many communities. In this talk, I will share early experiences designing and leading outreach activities, contributing to AIChE engagement, and teaching as a new faculty member. These efforts highlight strategies for fostering community, sparking curiosity, and building sustainable local connections. I aim to emphasize how outreach complements research and professional growth while inspiring the next generation of engineers.

topic: Deriving Fertilizer Micronutrients from Wastewater Using Polyelectrolyte Modified Nanofiltration Membranes
title: Deriving Fertilizer Micronutrients from Wastewater Using Polyelectrolyte Modified Nanofiltration Membranes
session_title: Emerging Stars: Elevating Early-Career Voices in Chemical Engineering through Innovation and Mentorship (Invited Talks)
abstract: In my talk, I will discuss a novel membrane surface-modification approach aimed at separating same sized, monovalent ions—ammonium (NH 4 + ) and potassium (K + ) from nutrient-rich sources such as anerobic digestates. NH 4 + and K + are two key nutrients which are in high demand as raw materials for fertilizer. This approach effectively contributes to circular economy principles by deriving value-added entities from waste and reducing the reliance on conventional energy intensive fertilizer raw material production processes. My talk will highlight the critical role of polyelectrolyte topology on the membrane separation performance using both synthetic and real wastewater matrices.
